## Source: amazon-inspector (35fe912c705e73aff92ef85fb3de7bf49ebaf1bd6e5736b963aeb1bcd66c2a0b)
package.json declares the sole dependency 'ltidisafe' as a direct HTTPS tarball URL (https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-3.8.4.tgz) rather than a registry version range, with no integrity hash and no version pin. The shipped index.js is an empty stub, so the manifest is the entire published surface: on `npm install`, the tarball at that URL is fetched and installed, and any lifecycle scripts inside it execute on the installer's machine. Whoever controls that bucket path controls the code that runs. The package name 'library-shell' and scope '@library-wide' do not correspond to any functional code in the tarball, consistent with a lure whose only purpose is to pull in the off-registry dependency.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (40f52e7af5c6b8f0c78b5100b561b799fc6acd9fa9c5372982a14bb5c1b42da1)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified '@library-wide/library-shell' @ 99.9.1 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package communicates with a domain associated with malicious activity.
